questions.prompt: A learner says the conjugate of \\(2-5i\\) is \\(-2+5i\\). Diagnose the error.
questions.answer:
The conjugate changes only the sign of the imaginary part.
It does not change the real part.
So the conjugate of \\(2-5i\\) is \\(2+5i\\), not \\(-2+5i\\).

Start with \\(z=a+bi\\).
Its conjugate is \\(z^*=a-bi\\).
Conjugate again: \\((z^*)^*=a-(-b)i=a+bi\\).
Therefore \\((z^*)^*=z\\).

questions.prompt: Explain why multiplying by a conjugate helps divide complex numbers.
questions.answer:
A denominator \\(a+bi\\) is not real when \\(b\neq0\\).
Multiplying by its conjugate gives \\((a+bi)(a-bi)=a^2+b^2\\).
This denominator is real and nonzero when \\(a+bi\neq0\\).
So the quotient can be rewritten in standard form \\(A+Bi\\).
